descriptions.text: The mint function relies on _isAuthorizedAddress(msg.sender) for access control. However, the registry variable used within _isAuthorizedAddress can be arbitrarily modified via the setRegistry function, which lacks proper access control. Vulnerable code snippet: Attack tx: https://app.blocksec.com/explorer/tx/eth/0x4019890fe5a5bd527cd3b9f7ee6d94e55b331709b703317860d028745e33a8ca?line=4 Analysis: To mint BBT, the msg.sender must pass the _isAuthorizedAddress check: The check queries the registry to validate whether the caller matches a known contract role: However, the registry itself can be reassigned by *any* external caller through the unprotected setRegistry function: This allows an attacker to set a malicious registry contract that returns their own address for one of the expected roles, thereby bypassing the authorization check and minting an arbitrary amount of BBT.

On 12 March 2024, BBT was exploited on Ethereum Mainnet due to a protocol logic flaw, resulting in a loss of approximately 5.06 ETH. The exploit allowed an attacker to bypass intended token minting restrictions and extract value by manipulating the registry and minting tokens, which were then swapped for ETH. The attack exploited a business logic flaw in BBT's registry and minting mechanism. The contract allowed an attacker to set an arbitrary registry and mint a large number of tokens without proper authorization checks.
